counting_unit: Three logical MAIN_RIV inventory groups; not three uniformly named channels or scalar-name approvals.

records.supported_name_scope: The complete selected path runs southeast from a northwestern headwater, south through the upper and middle corridor, then east and northeast after a southern bend to the New South Wales coast south of Lismore. Regional geometry is compatible with the Richmond River candidate, but the clearly legible Richmond River wording in Figure 4.22 is a basin callout. Possible blue river-line lettering in the retained regional maps is too indistinct to certify. Neither basin context nor geographic resemblance establishes a directly named representative river identity here. The whole group remains on a naming-scope hold after complete available-source/path review; the upper feeder, any river/storage interfaces, exact name transitions and coastal ending are unassigned at reach level.
limits: The Richmond River basin callout is context only; low-resolution possible line lettering is not certified as direct name evidence.
Richmond in the Sydney-area map is a town and is not evidence for the northern Richmond River candidate.
The regional publication is not a formal naming-register decision or surveyed contemporary mouth map.
Original HydroRIVERS source-coordinate equality and exact source reach-to-rendered-part name transitions are not verified.
No name is extended across generalized lake, estuarine, storage or coastal portions merely because they share a modeled group.

naming_scope_details.follow_up_scope: Obtain legible direct river-name evidence tied to the complete regional corridor before supporting the Richmond River representative identity. records.supported_name_scope: The complete three-fragment modeled mainstem begins in the southwest, sweeps east around a southern bend, then runs northeast through the upper/storage corridor and curves east toward the coast north of Sydney. The directly identified Hawkesbury River at Little Wobby photograph and the prose identifying Hawkesbury water supply to Richmond-Windsor, together with the full regional path comparison, support Hawkesbury River as a bounded representative system identity. The southwestern upper continuation follows the separately mapped Wollondilly corridor and the Lake Burragorang/Warragamba storage corridor. A modeled mainstem can include differently named feeder reaches. Coxs is a separately named contributor in source prose, not an assignment to a selected branch. Green water-transfer arrows in Figure 4.36 are not natural river geometry. Exact Wollondilly/storage/downstream name transitions, any Nepean or other intermediate naming, river/storage interfaces and the generalized coastal ending remain unassigned at reach level.
limits: Hawkesbury River basin wording alone is not the identity basis; a named river photograph and river-specific prose provide additional evidence.
Wollondilly and Lake Burragorang/Warragamba remain distinct upper/storage context. Coxs source prose and transfer arrows do not name selected reaches.
